citation.title: Error field optimization in DIII-D using extremum seeking control
citation.authors: M.J. Lanctot, K.E.J. Olofsson, M. Capella, D.A. Humphreys, N. Eidietis, J.M. Hanson, C. Paz-Soldan, E.J. Strait, M.L. Walker
citation.venue: unknown from text; extracted text says submitted to Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion, hint says Nucl. Fusion

topic: Closed-loop n=1 error-field correction on DIII-D using extremum seeking, with real-time CER rotation as the objective
own_question: Can an extremum-seeking loop find optimal I-coil currents within a single H-mode discharge?
actual_method_and_evidence: A Simulink-generated PCS algorithm applies a 5 Hz dither and uses real-time CER toroidal rotation of chord(s) as the objective. In one discharge (155601), it converged near known optimal currents after about 25 dither periods. A 0D momentum model was also simulated. No CES temperature, BES/ECEI, or nowcasting is involved.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Real-time CER analysis has been used inside a tokamak plasma control system as a control input (DIII-D rotation).
claim_checks.qualification: Applies to impurity rotation at DIII-D, not temperature or KSTAR; gives no latency or report-timing data.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: CER rotation is used as a real-time loop input; the source reports no arrival-time or latency numbers.
validation_if_relevant: Single-discharge demonstration plus a comparison discharge; no held-out validation.
forbidden_inferences: CES temperature nowcasting has been done
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional citation only, as an example of using real-time CER in a control loop. Its topic is error-field control, not temperature estimation.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
